slides.title: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
bullets: Class 10 — CBSE Social Science (History)

slides.speaker_notes: From a king's empire to a citizen's nation.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Trace the impact of the French Revolution and Napoleon.
Explain the role of the middle class + Romanticism.
Describe the 1830 and 1848 revolutions.
Outline the unification of Italy and Germany.
Interpret female allegories of nations.
Explain how nationalism led to WWI.

slides.title: Sorrieu's vision (1848)
bullets: Procession of peoples paying homage to LIBERTY.
Liberty: torch of Enlightenment + Charter of Rights.
Christ + saints look down — fraternity of nations.
Vision: world made up of democratic and social Republics.
Captures the political idea of the century.

slides.title: French Revolution (1789)
bullets: Sovereignty shifts from king to PEOPLE.
la patrie + le citoyen.
Tricolour flag replaces royal standard.
Estates General → National Assembly.
Uniform laws, weights, measures, currency.
French (Paris) becomes the national language.

slides.title: Napoleon's Civil Code (1804)
bullets: Abolished privileges based on birth.
Equality before the law.
Right to property secured.
In conquered lands: feudalism abolished, peasants freed.
Uniform laws, weights, measures, currency.

slides.title: But — costs and backlash
bullets: Conscription into the French army.
Censorship of newspapers and books.
Higher taxation in the conquered regions.
Loss of political freedoms.
Initial enthusiasm gave way to hostility.

slides.title: Two new social groups
bullets: EDUCATED MIDDLE CLASS — entrepreneurs, professionals, students.
Liberal demand: liberty + constitution + equality.
ROMANTICISM — emotion, intuition, folk culture.
Herder: true German culture lives in folk songs.
In partitioned Poland — Polish language as national resistance.

slides.title: 1830 — the wave begins
bullets: JULY REVOLUTION in France — Bourbons overthrown.
Louis Philippe installed; constitutional monarchy.
Belgium breaks away from the Netherlands.
Greek war of independence (1821–32).
Treaty of Constantinople (1832) recognises Greece.

slides.title: 1848 — revolutions across Europe
bullets: Food shortages + unemployment.
Uprisings in Paris, Vienna, Berlin, Italian states.
FRANKFURT parliament drafts a German constitution.
Friedrich Wilhelm IV rejects the crown.
Most uprisings defeated — but the demand stays.

slides.title: Women in 1848
bullets: Women organised political associations.
Founded newspapers, joined demonstrations.
Denied SUFFRAGE rights.
Admitted to Frankfurt parliament only as observers.
A long fight for women's suffrage begins.

slides.title: Unification — Germany
bullets: After 1848, conservatives lead state-building.
Bismarck of Prussia — three wars in seven years.
1864 — Denmark; 1866 — Austria; 1870-71 — France.
January 1871 — Wilhelm I crowned at Versailles.
Modern banking, currency, legal system.

slides.title: Unification — Italy
bullets: Italy was 7 states, no common language.
MAZZINI's Young Italy — failed.
CAVOUR + Victor Emmanuel II + French alliance defeat Austria (1859).
GARIBALDI's volunteers win the south (1860).
1861 — Victor Emmanuel II crowned king of UNITED ITALY.

slides.title: Britain — a different story
bullets: No British nation before the 18th century.
Identity was English, Welsh, Scot, Irish.
Act of Union 1707 — England + Scotland.
1801 — Ireland forcibly added.
Union Jack, 'God Save Our Noble King', English.

slides.title: Visualising the nation
bullets: Artists personified nations as women — ALLEGORIES.
MARIANNE — France: red cap, tricolour, cockade.
GERMANIA — Germany: crown of oak leaves (heroism).
Statues in public squares; image on coins, stamps.
Linked nation with motherhood, beauty, fraternity.

slides.title: Late nationalism + Balkans + WWI
bullets: Late 19th century — nationalism becomes narrow + intolerant.
European powers use it for IMPERIALIST aims.
Balkans = Slavs + Ottoman decline + ethnic mosaic.
Balkan states jealous of each other.
Great-power rivalry → FIRST WORLD WAR (1914).

bullets: 1. Two effects of Napoleon's Civil Code.

3. Three leaders of Italian unification.

5. Why is the Balkans called the 'powder keg' of Europe?

slides.title: Quick check
bullets: Q1. Marianne represents which country?
Q2. Bismarck — which country did he unite?
Q3. 1848 Frankfurt parliament — succeed or fail?
Q4. 1832 — what event?
Show fingers.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: 1789 French Revolution — nation as people, not king.
1804 Napoleonic Code — equality + property + uniform law.
Middle class + Romanticism = liberty + folk culture.
1830/1848 revolutions defeated, but demand stayed.
Italy 1861, Germany 1871 — by conservative state-building.
Late nationalism + Balkans → WWI 1914.
